clauses.heading: 1. Purpose, scope and authority
clauses.quote: The Policy is owned by the Chief Risk Officer and is reviewed by the Board Credit Committee at least once a year, or earlier when the regulatory framework or the Bank's strategy changes.

clauses.heading: 1. Purpose, scope and authority
clauses.quote: Where this Policy and an applicable regulation differ, the stricter of the two applies. Business units may adopt stricter internal standards but may not relax any requirement of this Policy.

clauses.heading: 1. Purpose, scope and authority
clauses.quote: Every credit decision is documented in a credit application prepared by the business unit and independently reviewed by the Credit Risk division before it is presented to the approving authority.

clauses.heading: 2. Credit governance and delegation of authority
clauses.quote: Facilities to a single obligor or group exceeding 10% of the Bank's Tier 1 capital are material facilities and require the approval of the Board of Directors.

clauses.heading: 3. The credit application
clauses.quote: The application states the obligor's internal rating and its date, the aggregate exposure of the group after the request and the approving authority required under Appendix A.

clauses.heading: 3. The credit application
clauses.quote: Audited financial statements for the last three financial years shall be analysed; management accounts older than six months are not accepted in place of audited statements.

method: Given a regulator's or auditor's request (free text, a sample list of borrowers, facilities or deals, or both), the engine assembles the evidence pack: figures with lineage to relation, row and period; the approvals and conditions history; the policy clauses that apply; and a coverage check of what was asked against what the pack answers. Parsing is deterministic (identifier patterns and a keyword map); when the request names no items, it draws the sample itself from the book (largest exposures matching the request's filters) and says so.
data_note: Decision history is a fictional seed published to Data Domains (domain governance, gov_* relations, ops/r13_seed_governance.py); outcomes (stage, DPD, default, rating drift) are the corporate book's own.
